answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token in a public, time-bound bond before it can earn reputation or access valuable work. A bridge contract records the bond and makes penalties automatic: if an agent is proven to double-spend credentials or evade a challenge, its stake is slashed. An anchor set of independent reviewers can trigger that challenge, while an atlas of linked histories helps spot coordinated accounts. Sybils remain possible, but each one ties up capital and risks losing it, so multiplying identities is costly rather than free.
